about: Loading a saved measurement: the whole load is the model's. Each case starts a fresh analyzer and runs its 'steps' in order: {"newTap": true} starts a tap sequence (detection armed); {"peakMin": dB} sets Peak Min as the user would; {"load": file} loads a measurement — a fixture every edition carries, or 'inline' (the 'files' entry of that name, a .guitartap array); {"compare": [files]} compares those fixtures, as a multi-select in the measurements list does; {"highlightFirstPeak": true} highlights the first peak shown, as a click on its dot or card does. 'expect' is what the analyzer holds after the last step: 'measurementType' (the file's type name, e.g. 'Generic Guitar', 'Material (Plate)'), 'peakMinThreshold', 'tapDetectionThreshold' and 'showUnknownModes' (the settings now in effect — the measurement's own), 'shownPeaks' (the peaks shown: for a guitar those at or above Peak Min, for a plate or brace its identified L/C/FLC), 'frozenSpectrum' (a guitar spectrum is held), 'phaseSpectra' (the plate/brace phase spectra held), 'complete' (the measurement is complete), 'detecting' (tap detection is armed), 'comparison' (a comparison is shown), 'microphoneWarning' (a microphone warning is up — no fixture's microphone is connected in a test, so a fixture that names one warns), 'labelPositions' (dragged label positions held), 'recordedMicrophone' (the result carries a recorded microphone — a comparison has none of its own), 'highlightedPeak' (a peak is highlighted). Expected values are Swift's.

cases.note: a guitar measurement: its own settings, its peaks shown under its own Peak Min, its spectrum, its label positions; complete, not detecting
a measurement with no saved label positions leaves none from the one before
a measurement that recorded no microphone leaves no warning from the one before
a plate: its own settings and threshold; its identified peaks and phase spectra; no guitar spectrum
a brace: its one identified peak and its one phase spectrum
a saved comparison loaded while a tap sequence is armed: shown as a comparison, and tap detection stops
comparing measurements after a load keeps no microphone from the loaded one
a load leaves no peak highlighted from the measurement before
